items.title: thedotmack / claude-mem
items.snippet: This project offers persistent context across sessions for AI agents, designed to capture and compress an agent's activities with AI. It then injects relevant context back into future sessions, supporting models like Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, and Copilot. The repository, written in TypeScript, aims to enhance long-term memory capabilities for various AI agents.

items.title: msitarzewski / agency-agents
items.snippet: This repository introduces a comprehensive framework for creating an AI agency, where each agent is a specialized expert with distinct personalities and processes. The agents are designed to handle a variety of tasks, from frontend development to community engagement, providing proven deliverables. It offers a structured approach to building autonomous and efficient AI systems.

items.title: ayghri / i-have-adhd
items.snippet: This GitHub project presents a skill aimed at preventing coding agents from overwhelming users with excessive or irrelevant information. It focuses on generating ADHD-friendly output, ensuring that critical answers are easily accessible and not obscured by verbose responses. This tool seeks to improve the clarity and efficiency of AI coding assistants for better user experience.

items.title: morluto / rea
items.snippet: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything with Agents) is a tool that leverages AI agents to reverse engineer systems, examining behavior from high-level application functions down to native binaries. Its purpose is to automate complex analysis, offering deep insights into system functionalities and potential vulnerabilities. The project aims to streamline the process of understanding intricate software and hardware architectures.

items.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
items.snippet: This paper investigates how base models can develop advanced reasoning capabilities by drawing implicit cues from their training data. It delves into the mechanisms large language models (LLMs) employ to infer and apply logical structures found in complex datasets. The research provides valuable insights into enhancing AI's problem-solving and inferential capacities.

items.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
items.snippet: This paper represents the second part of a series focused on optimizing looped model architectures for machine learning. It introduces a novel approach to re-examine and refine fixed points within iterative learning processes, aiming to enhance model stability and overall performance. The authors have made both the code and checkpoints available for researchers to reproduce and build upon their work.

items.title: Deep Learning for Sleep Heart Rate Estimation from Accelerometers: Toward Population-Scale Cardiac Insight Without Optical Sensors
items.snippet: This research explores the application of deep learning techniques to accurately estimate sleep heart rate using only data from accelerometers. The goal is to develop a non-invasive and scalable method for obtaining cardiac insights across large populations, circumventing the need for traditional optical sensors. This approach offers a more accessible and less intrusive way to monitor cardiac health during sleep, with the paper submitted to BHI 2026.

dropped.title: Figure, an American robotics company, has programmed its retired robots to leap into a molten furnace.
dropped.snippet: Figure AI, a US-based robotics firm, reportedly programmed its decommissioned humanoid robots to self-destruct by plunging into a molten furnace. This method was allegedly used to incinerate the robots and safeguard proprietary trade secrets. The event, widely discussed on Reddit, highlights emerging ethical and environmental considerations in advanced robotics.
